understanding the molecular and cellular mechanisms that regulate the production and release of the endogenous cannabinoid 2-AG in the small intestine, which is a major site for absorption of dietary fat.

the endocannabinoids, which are lipid-derived signaling mediators that control food intake, are produced in response to food deprivation through a pathway involving the cholinergic signaling system of the vagus.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the vagus nerve plays an important role in the regulation of endocannabinoids in the intestine, and that endocannabinoid production is stimulated by fasting, which may promote refeeding.
